chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to buy something, say: 'O Living, O Guardian, O Eternal, O Kind, O Merciful! I ask You by Your Honour and Your Power and what Your Knowledge encompasses, that You apportion for me from the trade today that which has the greatest sustenance, the widest grace, and the best outcome, for there is no goodness in that which has no good outcome.'
He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you buy an animal or a head (slave), say: 'O Allah, enable for me that it has the longest life, the most benefit, and the best outcome.'

key_terms.رَأْس: Head (referring to a slave or individual)

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when buying something in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a spiritual protocol for commerce, linking material transactions to divine sustenance (rizq) and ethical foresight. It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating dhikr into daily economic activities, ensuring that trade is not merely a worldly pursuit but a means of securing long-term benefit (khayr al-'aqibah). The specific invocation of Allah's attributes as 'The Ever-Living' and 'The Sustainer' underscores the dependence of all commercial success on Divine Will.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said,

‘Whenever you intend to buy something, so say, ‘O Living, O Guardian, Oh Eternal, O Kind, O Merciful! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Honour, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Power and what Your<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge eencompasses, that You<sup>azwj</sup> Apportion for me from the business today with a great sustenance, and extensive Grace, and its goodness being the end result, so there is no goodness in what there is no end result for it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever you buy an animal, or a head (slave), so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Enable for me the longevity of its life, and the abundance of its benefit, and the goodness of its end result’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When you decide to buy something say this, “O Living, O Guardian, O Eternal, O Compassionate, O Merciful I pray to You through Your majesty, Your power and all that Your knowledge encompasses, grant me of business the greatest share of sustenance, vastest extra favors and the best of consequences; there is no goodness in that which is void of good consequences.’”

He (the narrator) has said that abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘When you buy an animal or a head (living thing) say this, “O Allah, make it to live the longest, benefit the most and of the best consequences.’””
